title: RSL Companion consolidated account export
description: Payload POSTed to {ApiBaseUrl}/api/sync/consolidated/raw. One complete snapshot of one game account; a full replace, not a delta. Self-identifying: the server routes by the in-game accountId it carries. Human-readable contract and changelog: export-schema.md (keep both in sync, same commit).

x-relatedSchemas.clan: clan-export-schema.json — the account's clan record and roster; a SEPARATE payload to a separate endpoint, joined to this one on clanId.

accountId.description: In-game account id. The routing key; always equals account.accountId.

timestamp.description: ISO-8601 UTC instant the snapshot was taken.

uploaderVersion.description: Desktop app build that produced this payload. Stamped by the app, NOT by the extraction engine, so it is absent from engine-level dumps.

gameVersion.description: Live Raid build the snapshot was read from. Null when it could not be determined.

accountId.description: Duplicate of the top-level accountId; always equal.

resources.description: ALWAYS the complete allowlist (49 ids as of schema 3). Ids the account holds none of are present with quantity 0, so a missing id means the allowlist changed - never 'zero owned'. Join on id, NEVER on name: names track in-game renames (three changed in v1.5.4). NEVER ALL-ZERO: because every id is emitted unconditionally, a failed read returns a full-length array of zeroes rather than an empty one - so length proves nothing here and the `contains` constraint above is the real check. Every account holds at least some Silver, so at least one quantity is always non-zero. The uploader refuses to send an all-zero array; a consumer seeing one should discard the payload and keep what it has, never apply it (applying it zeroes the account's entire inventory).

id.description: Stable allowlist id. The only safe join key.

name.description: Display label. NOT stable across releases.

x-soulEconomy.description: Corrected in schema 3 / v1.5.4. Ids 10101, 10102, 10104, 10105, 10201 and 10204 are a DEFUNCT earlier soul system: they are not allowlisted, are never emitted, and must not be mapped onto the ids below - doing so is the bug v1.5.4 fixed.

ids.1111: Mortal Soul Coin (was 'Silver Soul Coin'; value was wrong before v1.5.4)
ids.1112: Immortal Soul Coin (was 'Gold Soul Coin'; value was wrong before v1.5.4)
ids.1113: Eternal Soul Coin (was 'Immortal Essence'; value was wrong before v1.5.4)
ids.10205: Eternal Essence (legacy; still emitted, semantics unverified)

heroes.description: The owned champion roster. NEVER EMPTY: the game gives every new player a starter champion, so there is no such thing as an account with zero. A zero-length array is therefore a failed read, not an empty roster — the uploader refuses to send one, and this constraint makes a consumer reject it rather than faithfully applying it and wiping the account's champions. Treat a validation failure here as 'discard this payload and keep what you have'.

name.description: Null when the champion index cannot resolve it.

instanceId.description: int64. Unique per OWNED COPY. Join key for factionGuardians and artifacts.

baseTypeId.description: Champion type, ascension digit stripped. Copies of one champion share this.

factionId.description: 0 when unresolved. Same id space as factionGuardians[].factionId.

blessingChosen.description: A blessing is equipped. Only ever true when awakeningLevel > 0.

isFactionGuardian.description: This copy is placed in an Academy guardian slot.

masteries.description: Always present and fully populated - deliberately verbose so consumers never null-check. Per-node metadata (name/tree/tier/cost) is intentionally absent: it is constant game data, joined from mastery_index.json in the RslCompanionMetadata repo.

selected.description: Chosen mastery node ids; empty array when none, never null. The id encodes position: 500*tree*tier*slot, tier being the tens digit.

totalScrolls.description: Unspent PLUS already spent on selected (each node's activation cost).

factionGuardians.description: Academy guardian slots. Each slot fuses up to TWO copies of one champion, hence the First/Second pair.

heroTypeId.description: Champion type WITH the ascension digit (366 = base 360 at ascension 6). Do NOT join this onto heroes[].baseTypeId.

heroBaseTypeId.description: Ascension stripped. THIS is what joins to heroes[].baseTypeId. The game's own field is misleadingly named HeroBaseTypeId but carries the ascension digit; both forms are published so consumers need not guess.

firstHeroInstanceId.description: Null when that half of the slot is empty.

secondHeroInstanceId.description: Null when that half of the slot is empty.

artifacts.description: The EQUIPPED-ARTIFACT MAP: which champion wears which artifact in which slot. Populated since schema 7 (~1.9k records on a mature account); before that it always arrived empty. CRITICAL: every stat field (setKindId, rankId, rarityId, primaryStatId, level) is 0 on EVERY record for EVERY account, because artifact stats live in Unity ECS component storage the extraction engine cannot decode. A 0 there means UNKNOWN, not a real value - rendering it as one shows an entire vault as rank-0/level-0 junk, and it must never overwrite previously-known-good stat data. Only artifactId, kindId and heroInstanceId carry real information. Covers EQUIPPED artifacts only: unequipped inventory is absent entirely, so never infer 'artifacts owned' from this array's length. May legitimately be empty for a brand-new account that has equipped nothing. RECONCILING WITH THE GAME: kindId 1-6 (Gear) and 7-9 (Accessories) are two separate in-game inventory categories and the game's own Artifacts counter covers GEAR ONLY, so this array's length matches no single on-screen number. Verified live 2026-07-31: 892 equipped gear + 1852 unequipped gear = the 2744 the game reported, while this array held 892 gear + 969 accessories = 1861. Filter to kindId <= 6 to compare, and expect equipped gear only.

artifactId.description: REAL. The equipped artifact's instance id; unique across the array (no artifact is worn twice).

kindId.description: REAL. The SLOT worn in: 1 Weapon, 2 Helmet, 3 Shield, 4 Gauntlets, 5 Chestplate, 6 Boots, 7 Ring, 8 Amulet, 9 Banner.

heroInstanceId.description: REAL. Joins to heroes[].instanceId. Omitted when 0.

setKindId.description: ALWAYS 0 - unknown, not 'no set'. See the array description.

rankId.description: ALWAYS 0 - unknown, not rank 0. See the array description.

rarityId.description: ALWAYS 0 - unknown, not a rarity. See the array description.

primaryStatId.description: ALWAYS 0 - unknown, not a stat id. See the array description.

level.description: ALWAYS 0 - unknown, not level 0. See the array description.

clanId.description: int64 id of the clan this account belongs to (the game calls a clan an Alliance). Null when the account is in no clan AND when the value could not be validated — this payload cannot distinguish the two, so never infer 'left the clan' from null. Stable and usable as a join key on its own: two accounts in the same clan report the same clanId. It is the ONLY clan field here because it is the only free one — a two-pointer read off the account data — whereas the clan's name and roster need a full-memory scan of the game (18-31s on a ~4s export) and are therefore a separate export: see clan-export-schema.json, which joins to this on clan.id.

scrollBalance.description: Mastery-scroll balance. ALWAYS carries all three rarities, defaulting to 0.
